I Never rested on the Muses bed,
Nor dipt my pen in Poesy's well;
But, since Heaven did me grace to breed
In a age when bad men write so well,
I strive to please, and not to offend,
The curious, by some new-found art;
For if I should my muse offend,
I fear my verse would ne'er be smart.

To William Drummond of Hawthornden

This transition came about following a significant event in his life: the unexpected passing of his mother, who was the sole supporter of his filmmaking aspirations. It was a significant blow when my mother, who was the only one in my family to support my passion for filmmaking, passed away. At that time, I was left with a void, a gaping hole in my heart, and I found it difficult to continue with my dreams. But I knew that she would want me to persevere, to keep pushing forward, and so I did. I picked myself up, dusted myself off, and continued to pursue my passion for filmmaking, determined to make her proud.
